question: Does the deep pair-selector ceiling survive giving hand controls the same larger planning budget?
selection: Choose one control per budget by lowest calibration mean cost subject to p95 of per-case median full planning times <= budget; freeze before fresh evaluation
oracle: Unchanged deep portfolio: affinity plus descent64; every unordered pair flipped then refined by two single-flip rounds; include incumbent
gate: For each budget: oracle median gain >=5%, bootstrap lower bound >0, frozen hand control p95 <=budget, and free perfect-selector full-path p95 <=budget; no GNN-specific claim
live_gate: 32 fresh cases, control5, control10 and oracle; 96 real HeROsim runs with all completions independently checked against SimPy even if screen fails
scope: Paired exploratory budget sensitivity, not independent replications; wall-clock planning excluded from simulated execution as in earlier gates; a positive screen still requires learnability and matched learned controls
